title: Putting a Deductible Recovery Right on the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
A deductible recovery taken from a host's Keyturn Host Payout Account is put right against what the protection enrolment behind it bears, because the recovery is only ever the host's own share of a settled loss and never more. Where a recovery has taken more than that, the sum over-recovered is put back onto the account by a correcting entry booked against the recovery entry that took it, and the host sees both lines on their statement.

## The handling action

The desk books the correcting entry itself. The entry names the earlier entry it corrects, carries the sum put back and is reported in the statement month it is booked in; the earlier entry is left exactly as it stands and the account's balance rises by the sum put back.

## Invoking the correction

The tool `post_recovery_correction_f20745c1` is unlocked and then called by the agent; it is the desk's own action on the host's account rather than something handed to the host to run.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `payout_account_id` | The reference number of the Keyturn Host Payout Account the correcting entry is booked to | An identifier, as returned by the payout account lookup for this host |
| `source_ledger_id` | The reference number of the earlier ledger entry being put right | An identifier, as returned by the payout ledger lookup for this account |
| `correction_amount` | The sum put back on the account by this correcting entry, in USD | A positive number rounded half to even to 2 decimal places; there is no empty value and no currency conversion, the account settling in USD throughout |

### Return

A single confirmation sentence in plain text. It carries the reference number of the new correcting entry, which is also the reference quotable for the correction, the reference number of the earlier entry it was booked against, and the sum put back in USD to 2 decimal places. The presence of that correcting entry reference is what indicates the money is back on the account.

## Points of judgement

**What is the correcting entry booked against?** The earlier entry that took the recovery, named by its own reference number.

**Is the earlier entry changed?** No. It is left exactly as it stands, and the correction appears as its own line.
